% rhythm: beamer frames under the class's default colours with each block's title and body grounds declared, so both engines paint them, top-aligned: a frame title into a painted block, its title to its body, out of it into a paragraph, a paragraph into a block, and one block to the next
% boundary: frametitle-block Larch span
% boundary: blocktitle-body Maple span
% boundary: block-par Oak span
% boundary: par-block Pine span
% boundary: block-block Rowan span
\documentclass{beamer}
\usepackage{fontspec}
\setsansfont{OpenSans-Regular.ttf}[Path=../corpus/fonts/, BoldFont=OpenSans-Bold.ttf, ItalicFont=OpenSans-Italic.ttf, BoldItalicFont=OpenSans-BoldItalic.ttf]
\setmainfont{OpenSans-Regular.ttf}[Path=../corpus/fonts/, BoldFont=OpenSans-Bold.ttf, ItalicFont=OpenSans-Italic.ttf, BoldItalicFont=OpenSans-BoldItalic.ttf]
\setbeamercolor{block title}{bg=black!10}
\setbeamercolor{block body}{bg=black!5}
\begin{document}
\begin{frame}[t]{Juniper title}
\begin{block}{Larch block}
Maple is the block's body.
\end{block}
Oak is the paragraph after the block.
\begin{block}{Pine block}
Quince is the second block's body.
\end{block}
\begin{block}{Rowan block}
Spruce is the third block's body.
\end{block}
\end{frame}
\end{document}
